`@assistant-ui/react` works with **React 18 and React 19**. The compatibility page says assistant-ui requires one of these, and React 16 and 17 aren't supported. `@assistant-ui/react-ink`, the terminal package, requires React 19.

**AssistantTransport** is built for this. It's a state-streaming protocol on top of `ExternalStoreRuntime`: your backend streams snapshots of its agent state (any JSON object), updated through `set` and `append-text` operations.

If your backend uses a framework with its own runtime, such as LangGraph or AG-UI, the selection guide says to use that instead. A reopened Assistant Cloud thread starts from `initialState` until your backend sends its state.

You need `setMessages` only if you want **branch switching**. `onNew` is the required handler, and the quickstart's adapter works without passing `setMessages`.

The reason is that your store owns the messages, while the runtime renders what you give it. UI features turn on according to which callbacks you provide. When a user switches branches, for example by clicking in BranchPicker, `setMessages` performs the switch by updating your messages.

- **Branch history:** a linear `messages` array assumes each message follows the previous one. For branching trees, build a `messageRepository` with `ExportedMessageRepository.fromBranchableArray()` and pass `setMessages` alongside it.
- **Saving the selection:** `unstable_onBranchChange` can persist the chosen branch, but doesn't enable switching by itself.
- **Other actions:** editing, regeneration and cancellation need `onEdit`, `onReload` and `onCancel`.

The troubleshooting section also lists missing `setMessages` under "State not updating", without explaining why. The docs don't say how the runtime computes the array it passes to `setMessages`.

To render reasoning yourself, use `MessagePrimitive.GroupedParts` and return your component for `case "reasoning"`, such as `<MyReasoning {...part} />`. For a shared wrapper, pass `groupBy={groupPartByType({ reasoning: ["group-chainOfThought", "group-reasoning"], "tool-call": ["group-chainOfThought", "group-tool"] })}` and render `children` in each group case. `part.status.type === "running"` on the reasoning group indicates streaming. Without grouping, `MessagePrimitive.Parts` takes a render function you can branch on; by default, reasoning renders nothing.

With this recommended approach, your chain-of-thought wrapper receives adjacent reasoning and tool calls as `children`; a text part closes the group.

The legacy `components.ChainOfThought` takes over all reasoning and tool-call rendering. It can't be combined with `Reasoning`, `ReasoningGroup`, `tools` or `ToolGroup`. Render reasoning through `ChainOfThoughtPrimitive.Parts` with `components={{ Reasoning }}`. It starts collapsed, but `Parts` doesn't track that, so gate it with `AuiIf` on `s.chainOfThought.collapsed`. The docs don't say what happens if `Reasoning` is omitted.
